---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

## Load script and directories
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(readxl)
library(stringr)
library(knitr)

# --- 1. Load and prepare data
data <- read_excel("full_merged_data_manual_fix.xlsx") %>%
  mutate(
    Lab_num = as.numeric(str_extract(join_id, "(?<=Lab_)\\d+"))
  )
data <- data %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(numeric_vars), ~ as.numeric(gsub(",", ".", gsub("[^0-9.,-]", "", .)))))


# Subset for variety tests
data_variety <- data %>%
  dplyr::filter(Location %in% c("Mendieta", "7H", "Caro Caido")) %>%
  mutate(Location = ifelse(Location %in% c("7H", "Caro Caido"), "CC/7H", Location)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(variety))

# --- 2. Define groups and numeric variables
all_groups <- c("Life_S", "Location", "region", "variety")
numeric_vars <- c(
  "Protein_mg_per_g_mean",
  "PE_mg_per_g_sample_mean",
  "carb_mg_per_g_mean",
  "ash_per_mean",
  "car_per"
)
chem_vars <- c("carb_mg_per_g_mean", "ash_per_mean", "car_per")

# --- 3. Kruskal-Wallis helper
get_kw_table <- function(dat, group_var, num_var) {
  res <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(num_var, "~", group_var)), data = dat)
  
  data.frame(
    Variable = num_var,
    Factor = dplyr::recode(group_var,
                            "Life_S" = "Life Stage",
                            "Location" = "Location",
                            "region" = "Region",
                            "variety" = "Variety"),
    DF = res$parameter,
    ChiSq = round(res$statistic, 2),
    P = format.pval(res$p.value, digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# --- 4. Generate combinations
combos <- expand.grid(Group = all_groups,
                      Variable = numeric_vars,
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# --- 5. Loop through and calculate Kruskal-Wallis for each
table6_kw <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(combos)), function(i) {
  grp <- combos$Group[i]
  var <- combos$Variable[i]
  
  dat <- if (grp == "variety") data_variety else data
  
  # Apply Lab 1-22 filter for carrageenan, ash, carbohydrate
  if (var %in% chem_vars) {
    dat <- dat %>% dplyr::filter(Lab_num <= 22)
  }
  
  get_kw_table(dat, grp, var)
})

# --- 6. Export and view
if (!dir.exists("results")) dir.create("results")
write.csv(table6_kw,
          "results/table6_style_summary_kw.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)

#--------#
#Make summary table too
# --- 3. Generate summary table (mean ± SE, N)


summary_table <- data %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(numeric_vars)) %>%
  summarise(across(
    everything(),
    list(
      mean = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      se = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(.x))),
      N = ~ sum(!is.na(.x))
    ),
    .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
  )) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = c("Variable", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "^(.*)_(mean|se|N)$"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Mean_SE = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", mean, se)
  ) %>%
dplyr::select(Variable, N, Mean_SE)

# --- 4. Display the table cleanly
kable(
  summary_table,
  caption = "General averages with standard error (mean ± SE) and sample size (N) for all numeric variables across the entire dataset."
)

```
